chapter: Will Vodery and the road shows
title: Directing 'Red Hot Harlem' with Will Morrissey
summary: Whaley describes Will Morrissey as white M.C. of the black revue 'Red Hot Harlem', the 'Penalty of Love' number whose two singers died, and Mae Barnes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No, let me go back to Will Morrissey. He was at the --
Who is Will Morrissey?
Morrissey was an old time comedian.
Black or white?

White man. He would have a high derby, a silk hat. And he would come out before the show and sit on the steps and entertain. And then he says, Tom, you ready? I says, all right. He says, let's go. That was stopping the traffic.
You were the musical director.
Yeah, I was directing the show.
And what was the name of that show?
Stopping the Traffic. Red Hot Harlem.
Red Hot Harlem.

Red Hot Harlem, that was it. Red Hot Harlem. That was back in -- it was around '28 or '29, '25, '27. Will Morrissey used to -- when I lived on 127th Street, he used to come up to my house, knock on the door at 4:00 in the morning, he and his wife. Li'l woman.
Will Morrissey.
Will Morrissey, I'll never forget him.
And he owned the show?
No, he didn't own the show. He was a --
Musical director, producer.
No, he was, like, an MC. He introduced the show.
It was a black show?
Yeah.
But he was a white man.
Yeah, Will Morrissey come on first. We had a skit in there, Walking the Last Mile. Roland Smith was doing it.
Who was Roland Smith?
Roland Smith was a singer.
Black man?
Yeah. And The Penalty of Love. And he --
The what of love?

Penalty. And he would sing this song and walk the last mile. And he'd go by the prisoners and they would holler, keep your head up, keep your chin up. And he would sing that. And he died. We had another guy do that same thing, and he died.
That was a bad luck role, wasn't it?
That was -- yeah. And I told the guy he should capitalize on this because it's two guys have died
doing that number, the Penalty of Love. And we had a girl singing -- oh, I can't think of her name. She's living. I met her recently. Barnes, Mae Barnes.
Mae Barnes. She lives out this way.
Yeah, Mae Barnes was in the show.
Mae Barnes. Great singer.
Oh, yeah, sure.
And Mae Barnes was in this show?
Yeah.
What did you say was the name of that show?
Red Hot Harlem.
Red Hot Harlem.
